column3: The Hebrew opens with a bare “I”; NKJV supplies “say,” and “the mouth of the king” is rendered “the king’s commandment.”
Close to the Hebrew; “stand in an evil matter” is rendered “take your stand for an evil thing.”
Close to the Hebrew; “will not know an evil thing” is rendered “will experience nothing harmful,” and “custom” “judgment.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the trouble of man is great upon him” is rendered “the misery of man increases greatly.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the wind” (ruach) is rendered “the spirit,” and “discharge in battle” “release from that war.”
Close to the Hebrew; “for evil to him” is rendered “to his own hurt.”
The Hebrew is difficult; NKJV follows the MT “they were forgotten” and “where they had so done,” while some versions read “praised.”
Close to the Hebrew; “is full in them” is rendered “is fully set in them.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV supplies “his days” and “surely.”
Close to the Hebrew; “gladness” is rendered “enjoyment,” and “to be glad” “be merry.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the task” is rendered “the business.”
Close to the Hebrew; “says he knows” is rendered “attempts to know.”
